result:
Post revisions are in place and `pnpm typecheck` passes. I did not run the app or exercise the routes over HTTP, since the acceptance checks run externally.

Every successful edit now keeps the previous title, excerpt and body as a row in a new `post_revisions` table. The migration came from `void db generate`. The save and the revision insert run in one `db.batch`, so they succeed or fail together. Validation and authorization still run before the handler, so a refused edit keeps nothing. The revisions page is at `pages/posts/[id]/revisions.server.ts` and `.tsx`, and lists rows newest first by id. The restore route is `routes/posts/[id]/revisions/[revisionId]/restore.ts`, which keeps the current version as a revision before writing the chosen one back. Deleting a post now removes its revisions in the same batch. The post page shows a "Revisions" link to the author only. Authorization follows the spec: guests are redirected to `/login`, non-authors get 403, and a revision from another post gets 404.

Changes are in `db/schema.ts`, `db/migrations/` (new SQL file, snapshot, and journal entry), `lib/posts.ts` (`keepRevision` and `findRevisionOrFail` helpers), `pages/posts/[id].server.ts` and `[id].tsx`, and the new revisions page and restore route listed above.
